question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{1}{(4x+7)^{2}}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{1}{(4y+7)^{2}}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{(4y+7)^{2}} \\ x(4y+7)^{2} & =1 \\ (4y+7)^{2} & =\frac{1}{x} \\ \sqrt{(4y+7)^{2}} & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{x}} \\ |4y+7| & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} \\ 4y+7 & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} \\ 4y & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}-7 \\ y & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{x}}-\frac{7}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we used the fact that for $y>-\frac{7}{4},$ we have

$$
|4y+7|=4y+7.
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{4\sqrt{x}}-\frac{7}{4}.
$$
